model.note: Part outlines are traced from John Deere's studio photo of an HD200 on a ProGator 2030A diesel (booms folded) and are approximate. The engine, filters, transaxle, pump, strainers, valves and the AgLeader controller are hidden and are in the parts list. Sprayer numbers come from the JD HD200/HD300 SelectSpray parts guide, vehicle numbers from the 2030A GPS ProGator parts guide TC588946 and OM omuc24452 (export). The recorded PIN 1TC200GXHNT130078 looks like the sprayer's own PIN: read the ProGator chassis plate before ordering engine or transaxle parts, and confirm which pump is fitted.

tank.name: Spray tank (757 L)
tank.desc: Polyethylene tank rated 757 L, with jet agitation through a proportional valve (7.9 mm orifice). Rinse the tank, pump, boom and nozzles with clean water after every job and clean the fill basket strainer. A failed pump diaphragm puts spray mix into the pump oil: milky oil in the pump sight glass means replace the diaphragms now (club practice). The sprayer is removable from the ProGator and uses the ProGator speed sensor.

hoses.name: Spray hoses and clamps
hoses.desc: Inspect hoses and clamps every 50 h or weekly (club practice). The diaphragm pump is positive displacement: the relief valve must be set (start at 13.8 bar / 200 psi). Dead-heading the pump without relief damages hoses and pump.

rack.name: Boom centre frame, fold and lift
rack.desc: Carries both booms and the boom lift. Every 50 h or weekly (club practice): grease the sprayer pivots and boom hinges, check the boom breakaways and test the boom lift and section valves. Check the breakaways before each job.

boomL.name: Spray boom, left (folded in this photo)
boomL.desc: 3-way nozzle bodies PM42W7 on a 1/2 in. boom clamp, each with check-valve diaphragm PM4DCVAE (comes with the body): replace the diaphragm if a nozzle drips after shut-off. Before each job check every nozzle for pattern and blockage. Every 3 months catch-test every nozzle and replace any tip more than 10 % off nominal or off the average (club practice). Grease the boom hinges every 50 h.

boomR.name: Spray boom, right (folded in this photo)
boomR.desc: 3-way nozzle bodies PM42W7 on a 1/2 in. boom clamp, each with check-valve diaphragm PM4DCVAE (comes with the body): replace the diaphragm if a nozzle drips after shut-off. Before each job check every nozzle for pattern and blockage. Every 3 months catch-test every nozzle and replace any tip more than 10 % off nominal or off the average (club practice). Grease the boom hinges every 50 h.

pump.name: Sprayer pump (diaphragm)
pump.desc: Driven by a hydraulic motor off the ProGator hydraulics. Two pumps are offered: diaphragm, 113.9 L/min and 20 bar max (relief set 13.8 bar), or centrifugal, 367 L/min and 6.6 bar. The parts here are for the diaphragm pump: check which is fitted. The diaphragm pump pistons run in an oil bath: check the oil in the sight glass before each job. The pump oil spec and capacity were not found: confirm with the dealer. Replace the diaphragms (kit TCA19675) and O-rings (TCA19677) every 400 h or yearly, whichever comes first, and inspect the check valves while the pump is open. Grease the pump with JD Moly High Temp EP grease. Overhaul kit TCA19680. TCA19676 is a valve kit in the parts guide but a repair kit on the JD shop and at Emmetts: confirm what is in it before ordering.

strainer.name: Suction strainer and pressure filter
strainer.desc: Clean the suction strainer after every job and replace the screen if torn. The Emmetts price for TCA19413 looks like a full assembly: ask for the screen only. The 100-mesh self-cleaning filter on the pressure side: check it before each job.

valves.name: Rate valve, boom section valves and process valve
valves.desc: Boom control (proportional rate) valve TCA26145 from sprayer S/N 055169 (TCA19696 up to 055168). The recorded PIN ends 130078: if that is the sprayer PIN it is after the break, so TCA26145. Three boom section metered bypass valves TCA19695: adjustable throttling valves, set so the boom pressure stays the same when sections switch. Manual process valve seal kit AMT2247. Check the relief valve setting (13.8 bar / 200 psi to start) every 50 h.

controller.name: AgLeader InCommand rate control
controller.desc: GPS rate control fitted to this sprayer. Club history: a spray-volume fault; Brandt hydraulic testing cleared the JD system and pointed to the AgLeader flow control (escalated to Position Partners). Rate control depends on the flow meter calibration, the speed input and the rate valve TCA26145: check those three together. Before spraying confirm pressure and rate against a known catch test. Every 3 months (club practice): check the flow meter against a timed catch at known pressure, check the speed input to the controller and record the results with the spray records.

rops.name: ROPS and seat belts
rops.desc: Check the ROPS, seat belts and any loose or damaged parts before each use (OEM daily checks).

seats.name: Seats
seats.desc: The seat switch is one of the safety interlocks with the park brake, neutral and the auxiliary hydraulic switch: check them before each use (OEM).

steering.name: Steering wheel
steering.desc: Check the steering and control cables before each use. Check toe-in every 500 h or yearly (dealer / technical manual).

hood.name: Front hood and grille
hood.desc: After each use clean debris off the machine and out of the cooling system, including the radiator screen (OEM).

lights.name: Headlights
lights.desc: Headlights and indicators in the front hood. 12 V system, battery TY25876B (see Battery).

bumper.name: Front bumper
bumper.desc: Check for loose or damaged parts before each use (OEM daily checks).

fenderF.name: Front fender and side panel
fenderF.desc: Check tyres, pressures and wheel hardware before each use (OEM daily checks).

fenderR.name: Rear fender
fenderR.desc: Rear fender under the sprayer. After washing, grease the fittings (OEM after-use checks).

chassis.name: Frame, cargo bed and lower body
chassis.desc: Carries the sprayer on the cargo bed. Grease after washing: vehicle grease is JD Multi-Purpose HD Lithium Complex or SD Polyurea. Check for leaks, loose or damaged parts before each use. Record the ProGator chassis PIN separately from the sprayer PIN: engine and transaxle parts are ordered against the chassis.

tyreFL.name: Front tyre, left
tyreFL.desc: Check tyres and pressures before each use (pressure table in OM omuc24452). Check wheel hardware at the 50 h break-in.

tyreFR.name: Front tyre, right
tyreFR.desc: Check tyres and pressures before each use (pressure table in OM omuc24452). Check wheel hardware at the 50 h break-in.

tyreR.name: Rear tyre
tyreR.desc: Check tyres and pressures before each use (pressure table in OM omuc24452). Check wheel hardware at the 50 h break-in.

engine.name: Engine: Yanmar 3TNV80F diesel
engine.desc: 3-cylinder, 1,267 cc, liquid cooled (export OM). Oil 2.1 L with filter: JD Plus-50 II (10W-30 in the 2023 parts guide, 15W-40 in the earlier guide) or Torq-Gard Supreme. Change oil and filter M806418 every 200 h or yearly. At 200 h also check the alternator belt (10 mm deflection), hoses and clamps and the air intake for leaks. Dealer: injectors and valve clearance at 1500 h, injection pump at 3000 h or 36 months. The OEM list also has "inspect timing belt" (200 h) and "replace PCV valve" (800 h); the timing belt job is marked gas-only: confirm with the dealer what applies to the diesel. Hour meter about 1,070 h (Oct 2026): next oil at 1,200 h, 500 h service and injectors/valves at 1,500 h.

oilfilter.name: Engine oil filter
oilfilter.desc: Change with the oil every 200 h or yearly (2.1 L JD Plus-50 II).

aircleaner.name: Air cleaner
aircleaner.desc: Primary element M131802 every 300 h or yearly, secondary M131803 every 500 h or yearly (parts guide). OM: only open the canister for scheduled service; replace an element if very dirty or damaged.

fuel.name: Fuel tank and filter
fuel.desc: Diesel tank 30.66 L. Replace the fuel filter element MIU804763 in the sediment bowl every 500 h or yearly: close the fuel tap and clean the bowl. The bowl and head assembly MIA884996 is only needed if damaged. Check the fuel/water separator before each use.

transaxle.name: Transaxle and hydraulic oil, filter and strainer
transaxle.desc: One oil serves the transaxle and hydraulics: 10.6 L JD Hy-Gard J20C (or Bio Hy-Gard); never engine oil or type F ATF. Filter M131053 at the 50 h break-in, then oil and filter every 500 h or yearly. Clean the transaxle oil strainer M800489 (left side) at each oil change and replace it if damaged; drain plug 49 N.m. There is no separate transmission filter. These hydraulics also drive the sprayer pump motor.

frontaxle.name: Front axle and drive shaft (4WD models)
frontaxle.desc: 4WD models only: check the front axle oil every 100 h and change it every 500 h (3.3 L JD Hy-Gard J20C). Grease the 4WD drive shaft (3 fittings, SD Polyurea). Check whether JD Sprayer 1 is 4WD.

cooling.name: Radiator, coolant and thermostat
cooling.desc: 3.8 L JD Cool-Gard II pre-mix (or Cool-Gard II PG pre-mix). Check the level before each use. Change coolant and thermostat every 2000 h or 24 months. Clean the radiator screen after use.

belt.name: Water pump and alternator belt
belt.desc: V-belt MIU800108 (2030A parts guide). Check at the 50 h break-in and every 200 h: 10 mm deflection.

brakes.name: Brakes
brakes.desc: DOT 3 brake fluid (wet boiling point at least 140 C). Check the fluid level at the 50 h break-in; flush the lines and replace the fluid every 2000 h or 24 months. Check the brakes and park brake before each use.

battery.name: Battery
battery.desc: Battery TY25876B (2030A parts guide). Clean and check every 100 h.

TCA19696.name: Boom control (rate) valve, sprayer S/N up to 055168
TCA19696.note: Earlier sprayers only. From S/N 055169 the valve is TCA26145.

M801101.name: Fuel filter element (older ProGator guide)
M801101.note: Listed in an older ProGator parts guide; the 2030A guide lists MIU804763.

TCA19676: Pump valve kit (QRG) / 'diaphragm pump repair kit' (JD shop)
TCA26145: Boom control (proportional) valve — S/N 055169 and later
MIA884996: Fuel filter assembly (bowl/head) — only if damaged
